stem: An adolescent has a harsh, loud, high-pitched, monophonic sound best heard over the neck on inspiration; which airway sound is this?
explanation: Stridor is the correct label for a harsh, loud, high-pitched, monophonic inspiratory sound best heard over the neck.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because wheeze is typically a musical expiratory sound best heard over the chest.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because stridor is a harsh, high-pitched, monophonic inspiratory sound best heard over the neck.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because stertor is a low-pitched snoring sound from the upper airway, usually due to nasal or pharyngeal obstruction.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because secretions produce coarse, wet, bubbling sounds rather than a discrete inspiratory neck sound.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because habit cough is a coughing pattern, not an inspiratory airway sound.
